how students’ epistemological beliefs are shaped in the process of knowledge building.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
students’ epistemics were built in the knowledge building environment, and this is an important finding for the future of education in the 21st century.

the knowledge building approach can help students to build their epistemic repertoire, which is the ability to engage in self-directed learning, to be collaborative learners, and to do more idea work, as well as to construct knowledge together with others.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the students in the KBC were able to build their knowledge in a more self-directed and collaborative manner, and the knowledge they built were at higher levels than those in the non-KBC.
we have demonstrated that the knowledge building approach is a powerful approach to build students’ social and epistemic competencies for learning and teaching.
the knowledge building approach has the potential to enhance students’ epistemics and their engagement in learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students can be taught to build knowledge in a community and to develop their epistemic repertoire in Social Studies.
students in the KBC were able to build their own knowledge with the support of the teachers, the knowledge building community and the Knowledge Forum.
teachers should not just teach students how to use technology to support learning, but to use technology to help students learn how to think, to learn, and to collaborate.
